businessModel: Regional facilities management services provider, 280 employees, $32M revenue

ownerIntake.businessType: Facilities management (HVAC, maintenance, cleaning) serving commercial real estate and corporate campuses across Southeast. $32M revenue, EBITDA 11.5% ($3.68M), down from 14% two years ago. Gross margin 28% (down from 31%). Labor cost increases (+14% in two years) outpacing pricing power.
ownerIntake.stage: Mature: margin compression and growth slowdown. Revenue +3% YoY (vs. 8% historical), EBITDA margin declining. Customer concentration: top 5 = 40% of revenue. Utilization 82% (tight), technician turnover 22% annually.
ownerIntake.ownerGoal: Restore EBITDA to 14%+ within 18 months through operational efficiency and customer mix optimization.
ownerConstraints: Labor shortage: technician wages +14% in 24 months; tight labor market. Automation capex needed but uncertain ROI.
Pricing pressure: Large customers (top 5 = 40% of revenue) push back on rate increases; price increases limited to 3-4% annually vs. cost increases 6%+ annually.
Service complexity: Customers expect higher service levels (faster response, higher quality) without paying premium. Scope creep consuming margin.
Competitive landscape: National FM companies entering markets with scale advantages; regional consolidation trend.
ownerIntake.immediateConcern: EBITDA margin eroding (14% → 11.5%) while revenue growth stalls (3% YoY vs. 8% historical). Labor cost inflation (+14%) outpaces pricing power (3-4%). Technician turnover (22%) increasing, creating training burden. Customer concentration (40%) creates risk. Must determine whether problem is pricing/customer mix or operational efficiency.

evidence.finding: EBITDA margin down 250bps (14% → 11.5%), gross margin down 300bps (31% → 28%). Revenue growth slowing (3% vs. 8% historical). Operating leverage negative: costs rising faster than revenue.
Labor costs +14% in 24 months while pricing power limited (3-4% annual increases). Technician turnover 22% consuming hiring/training resources.
